segments.narration: Astronauts spotted giant black circles stamped into Siberian lake ice. In 2009, space station photos revealed massive dark rings on Lake Baikal.
segments.visual_query: lake baikal aerial frozen winter ice

segments.narration: The ice was four feet thick, yet these rings stretched four miles wide. Declassified satellite images showed they had quietly appeared for decades.
Locals avoided them, fearing the lake floor was venting toxic gas. What could carve perfect miles-wide circles into solid ice?
In 2020, scientists lowered deep-water probes beneath the surface. They found warm underwater currents, driven by hydrothermal vents, swirling into massive thermal eddies.
segments.visual_query: underwater thermal probe scientific research ice

segments.narration: These underwater whirlpools melt the ice from below, creating giant lens-like rings visible from space.
segments.visual_query: lake baikal aerial ice patterns winter
